text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Politician Tassos Papadopoulos has been knocked out of the presidential candidate race by communist Akel leader Demetris Christofias. President Glafcos Clerides will clarify his own intentions in autumn.
- A 60-year-old cement factory worker met with a tragic death after an explosion in a pressurised cement container in Limassol.
- Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou will table a proposal to cabinet for a 2 million pound ($3.9 million) cash injection to the state-run Cyprus Broadcasting Corporation.
- President Clerides is sceptical on the settlement talks prospects.
- New strike threat looms at Cyprus Airways as pilots gave their union the go-ahead to take measures preventing disciplinary procedures against three captains.
- Akel will decide at the end of June on what candidate to support during the presidential elections.
- Political party leaders will possibly accompany the president to New York where direct talks with the Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash are due to start on July 9.

- Turkey adds to the climate of pessimism at the upcoming talks with new statements warning that the occupied areas will receive recognition (as a Turkish Cypriot state) in a few years if the Cyprus issue is not solved.
- Crime gangs have been preparing for an all-out war with their rivals to have exclusive rights over the proceeds from criminal rackets in the Larnaca area.

- An attempt at cooperation between Akel and centre-right Diko in the presidential elections crumbles. Now an intensive round of consultations is due to start between Diko, rightwing Disy and the presidential palace on possible cooperation.
